Oil has been produced in the Republic of the Congo since 1957, mostly from fields off Pointe-Noire, and since the 1970s it has made up most of the country's exports and state income.

The French company Elf ran most fields, even under the Marxist regime. Oil money paid for a large civil service and for the rivalry of the politicians who fought over it, and borrowing against future oil left heavy debts.

The struggle for control of oil revenue fed the civil war of 1997, and Sassou Nguesso has relied on it since. Pointe-Noire became the economic capital, while most Congolese stayed poor.
